routes.label: Count matching odd or even numbers

question: Ten balls numbered \(1\) to \(10\) are in a jar. Jack reaches into the jar and randomly removes one of the balls. Then Jill reaches into the jar and randomly removes a different ball. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers on the balls removed is even?
solution:
The sum is even exactly when both numbers are odd or both are even. Initially, the jar contains \(5\) odd-numbered balls and \(5\) even-numbered balls.

If Jack draws an odd number, \(4\) of the \(9\) remaining balls are odd. If he draws an even number, \(4\) of the \(9\) remaining balls are even. These two cases cover every possible first draw, and in either case exactly \(4\) of Jill's \(9\) equally likely choices give an even sum.

Therefore the probability is \(\boxed{\frac49}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
